facts.statement: The species Fresnosaurus drescheri was first described by Welles in 1943.
facts.quote: The type species is Fresnosaurus drescheri, first described by Welles in 1943.

facts.statement: The genus name Fresnosaurus honors Fresno County, and the species name honors Arthur Drescher.
facts.quote: The generic name Fresnosaurus honors Fresno County, while the specific name honors Arthur Drescher.

facts.statement: Fresnosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) in what is now California.
facts.quote: Fresnosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) of what is now California.

facts.statement: Fresnosaurus likely ate small bony fish, belemnites, and ammonites.
facts.quote: Like all elasmosaurid plesiosaurs, it probably ate small bony fish, belemnites, and ammonites.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was a juvenile with unusually massive proportions, an unusual coracoid, and an unusual humerus compared to Aphrosaurus.
facts.quote: el fósil era un ejemplar juvenil de "proporciones más masivas" que Aphrosaurus, con un coracoide y húmero inusuales.

facts.statement: Fresnosaurus is classified in the family Elasmosauridae.
Fresnosaurus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Fresnosaurus was probably at least 9 meters (30 feet) long.
rejected.quote: Fresnosaurus was probably at least 9 meters (30 feet) in length.
